title: Endomorphism fibres: additive coordinates, coherent shifts and strict augmentations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with integer cochain complexes, cones and shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consider the category whose objects are pairs $(V,s)$ with $V$ a cochain complex and $s:V\to V$ a chain endomorphism, and whose morphisms $a:(V,s)\to(W,t)$ are chain maps satisfying $as=ta$, with componentwise composition and addition. Set $K(V,s)=\operatorname{Cone}(s)[-1]$. The reordered cone coordinates identify
$$K(V,s)^q=V^q\oplus V^{q-1},\qquad d(v,u)=(dv,-du-sv).$$
The diagonal formula $K(a)(v,u)=(av,au)$ defines an additive functor on this category. Shifting $(V,s)$ means $(V[r],s[r])$. There are coherent natural chain isomorphisms
$$\sigma_{(V,s),r}:K(V[r],s[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}K(V,s)[r],\qquad(v,u)\mapsto(v,(-1)^r u)$$
for every integer $r$, with inverse given by the same coordinate formula. Under the canonical degree reindexings, $\sigma_0$ is the identity and the successive comparisons for $r$ and $r'$ agree with the comparison for $r+r'$.
For every complex $M$ and chain map $J:M\to V$ with $sJ=0$, the formula $\eta_J(m)=(Jm,0)$ is a chain map $M\to K(V,s)$. If $a:(V,s)\to(W,t)$, $J':M'\to W$ satisfies $tJ'=0$, and $g:M\to M'$ satisfies $aJ=J'g$, then $K(a)\eta_J=\eta_{J'}g$. For every $r$ the same specified shift comparison satisfies
$$\sigma_{(V,s),r}\eta_{J[r]}=\eta_J[r].$$
These formulas are identities of biproduct component morphisms and apply without boundedness or exactness assumptions.

source.place: Cones paragraph, functorial fibre and shifts. Coordinate conventions: Stacks Tag 014E (derived.tex, definition-cone) and Tag 011G (homology.tex, definition-shift-cochain).

proof.text: Work throughout with biproduct component morphisms: a displayed pair denotes the two projections of a map from an arbitrary object, not elements of an object of $\mathcal A$. By [def-sp-abelian] finite biproducts and bilinear composition exist. For intertwining chain maps $a,b$, the identities $(ba)s=b(ta)=(bt)a$ and $(a+a')s=ta+ta'=t(a+a')$ show closure under composition and addition; identities and zero maps intertwine as well. Associativity, units and the abelian-group laws on morphisms are inherited componentwise from complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This gives the stated preadditive category of pairs.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone: the two by two cone differential

proof.text: By the cone convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\operatorname{Cone}(s)^{q-1}=V^{q-1}\oplus V^q$ has differential $(u,v)\mapsto(du+sv,-dv)$. The shift $[-1]$ negates this differential. Reordering its two summands therefore gives $K(V,s)^q=V^q\oplus V^{q-1}$ and $D(v,u)=(dv,-du-sv)$. Directly, $D^2(v,u)=(0,dsv-sdv)=(0,0)$ since $s$ is a chain map. Reordering is the biproduct permutation, whose inverse is the same permutation.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone: the two by two cone differential

proof.text: For an intertwiner $a:(V,s)\to(W,t)$, put $K(a)=\operatorname{diag}(a,a)$. Then $D_WK(a)(v,u)=(d_Wav,-d_Wau-tav)$ and $K(a)D_V(v,u)=(ad_Vv,-ad_Vu-asv)$. They agree by the chain-map identity for $a$ and $ta=as$, so $K(a)$ is a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On both biproduct components, $K(1)=1$, $K(ba)=K(b)K(a)$, $K(a+a')=K(a)+K(a')$ and $K(0)=0$. Thus these object and morphism formulas give an additive functor; these equalities use only bilinearity and biproduct projections [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone: the two by two cone differential

proof.text: Let $\epsilon_r=(-1)^r$ for an arbitrary integer $r$, so $\epsilon_r^2=1$. Using the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and Tag 011G, at the reindexed degrees the source $K(V[r],s[r])$ has differential $(v,u)\mapsto(\epsilon_r dv,-\epsilon_r du-sv)$ and the target $K(V,s)[r]$ has differential $(v,u)\mapsto(\epsilon_r dv,-\epsilon_r du-\epsilon_r sv)$. For $\sigma_r(v,u)=(v,\epsilon_r u)$, both $D_{\mathrm{target}}\sigma_r(v,u)$ and $\sigma_rD_{\mathrm{source}}(v,u)$ equal $(\epsilon_r dv,-du-\epsilon_r sv)$. Hence $\sigma_r$ is a chain map; its square on components is $(v,\epsilon_r^2u)=(v,u)$, giving the specified inverse.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain: integer shift differential and shifted maps

proof.text: For each intertwiner $a$, both $K(a)[r]\sigma_{(V,s),r}$ and $\sigma_{(W,t),r}K(a[r])$ send $(v,u)$ to $(av,\epsilon_r au)$, proving naturality. The shift maps simply reindex the components of $a$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. At $r=0$, $\epsilon_0=1$, so the comparison is the identity. Starting at $K(V[r][r'],s[r][r'])$, first apply $\sigma_{(V[r],s[r]),r'}$, then $\sigma_{(V,s),r}[r']$. The resulting coordinates are $(v,\epsilon_r\epsilon_{r'}u)=(v,\epsilon_{r+r'}u)$, since $(-1)^{r+r'}=(-1)^r(-1)^{r'}$ for all integers. Under the canonical reassociation of degree indices this is exactly $\sigma_{(V,s),r+r'}$, as required.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain: integer shift differential and shifted maps

proof.text: For $J:M\to V$ with $sJ=0$, $D\eta_J(m)=(d_VJm,-sJm)=(Jd_Mm,0)=\eta_Jd_M(m)$; thus $\eta_J$ is a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Given $aJ=J'g$ and $tJ'=0$, the two maps $K(a)\eta_J$ and $\eta_{J'}g$ have components $(aJ,0)=(J'g,0)$. Finally $s[r]J[r]=(sJ)[r]=0$, and $\sigma_{(V,s),r}\eta_{J[r]}$ has components $(J[r],\epsilon_r0)=(J[r],0)$, which are precisely those of $\eta_J[r]$. Equality of the two biproduct projections gives each claimed equality of morphisms [def-sp-abelian]. All arguments are degreewise finite biproduct calculations; they impose no boundedness or exactness conditions.
